A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KungfuBot/PBHC work and contain 28 pages, including Appendices A–F. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a complete comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation comparisons, motion-processing studies, and Unitree G1 experiments in Section 5, including ten real-world Tai Chi trials. Appendix E contains additional empirical analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation and robot experiments in Section 5 and Appendix E, including the results in Tables 1, 2, 12, and 13.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C preserve the same motion-processing pipeline, adaptive tracking-factor updates, actor-critic architecture, rewards, curricula, and control procedures.

E1.justification: Both use the same 13-motion collection drawn from videos, AMASS, and LAFAN (Table 4). Motion-filtering, contact-estimation, simulation, and real-world task coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains OmniH2O, ExBody2, MaskedMimic (Oracle), and the PBHC oracle variant. Comparator membership also matches in Figure 10 and the tracking-factor and contact-mask ablations.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, 1,000-episode evaluations, preprocessing, model sizes, training budgets, and deployment procedures remain identical in Section 5 and Appendices B–D.

E4.justification: The filtering study, fixed-factor ablations, learning curves, contact-estimation and motion-correction analyses, and contact-mask ablations are unchanged (Sections 5.2, 5.4, 5.6 and Appendix E).

E5.justification: Both retain three random training seeds, ten Tai Chi trials, mean and standard-deviation reporting, and Table 1's two-sided permutation tests at p < 0.05.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, curves, and qualitative demonstrations match throughout. For example, Table 2 retains Tai Chi root-relative body-position errors of 33.18 ± 2.720 mm in MuJoCo and 36.64 ± 2.592 mm on the real robot.

T1.justification: The bi-level formulation in Section 3.2 and optimal tracking-factor derivation in Appendix A retain identical assumptions and mathematical reasoning. Other equations and formal definitions also match.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning physics-based motion processing, adaptive tracking, tracking accuracy, and highly dynamic Unitree G1 deployment.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations of absent environment awareness and one motion per policy; Appendix F's broader-impact discussion also matches.

D1.justification: The abstract's displayed and embedded project-page address changes from kungfu-bot.github.io to kungfubot.github.io, revising resource access information. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and training times remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish improved resource availability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning relative to prior approaches, and all 58 bibliography entries remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page project URL and arXiv version/date stamp are edited. Wording, terminology, section ordering, and appendix structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–13 retain identical graphics, structure, captions, and placement. Rendered pages 2–28 are pixel-identical; page 1 preserves its layout around the URL and version-stamp edits.

improvement.justification: Both versions provide identical scientific evidence, reasoning, limitations, and exposition, including all appendices. The project-address and arXiv-stamp edits leave the paper's documented quality essentially unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that the address change resolves an access problem or provides additional resources.
